Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are out in the middle and the West Indies players can be seen in a huddle before taking their places on the field. Ben Duckett and Jamie Smith, the opening duo for England, wait patiently near the boundary ropes before making their way out to the middle. It will be Akeal Hosein to take the new ball as he so often does for the Windies. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, 47 runs in the last two overs, and a total of 75 runs in the last 4 overs for West Indies and that has changed the make of this game completely. England do have the batting to gun this target down and it should be a very exciting chase. Stay tuned as the run chase is up next.

Things changed quickly in the final 5-6 overs as Rovman Powell took the bull by the horns and played a stellar cameo to re-ignite the innings. After he fell, Jason Holder and Romario Shepherd went berserk in the 19th over, smashing Adil Rashid for a total of 5 sixes and that really shifted the momentum. The Windies were able to pick up a few more boundaries in the final over and ended the innings on a high.

The middle phase was where the hosts came roaring back into the game and once they saw the back of Shai Hope, they managed to put on the squeeze. Charles did start to get a move on but played too many shots and got out and the Windies' scoring rate was hovering under the 8 runs per over mark.

West Indies were put into bat by Harry Brook, but their innings got off to the worst possible start. Evin Lewis fell on the very first ball as Johnson Charles struggled for timing in the Powerplay. It was a thunderous knock from Shai Hope that ensured the Windies had a fruitful Powerplay. For England, Luke Wood bowled a couple of fine overs as the others went the distance early on.

Now, that is a more than competitive total on the board and West Indies will be ecstatic heading into the innings break. England would have taken a score around 170 runs and even that would have been more than they were staring at around the 13th-14th over mark, but 197 is definitely going to be a difficult chase, even with their batting lineup.

Wood just strides in from over the wicket and darts a straight yorker in perfectly towards middle stump. Evin Lewis is taken aback and ends up playing all around it. UltraEdge shows that the bat hit the ground and not the ball and Ball Tracking comes up with three reds. A golden duck here for Lewis!

In all readiness for this second T20I to commence here in Bristol! Simon Doull on air mentions that it is quite breezy out there. Overcast skies welcome the two umpires and the players. The players of England spread out to the field and out walk the two openers for West Indies - Evin Lewis and Johnson Charles. Luke Wood, back in the English side, will bowl the first over of the match. Off we go...

West Indies (Playing XI) - Evin Lewis, Johnson Charles, Shai Hope (C/WK), Roston Chase, Sherfane Rutherford, Romario Shepherd, Jason Holder, Rovman Powell, Gudakesh Motie, Alzarri Joseph, Akeal Hosein (In for Andre Russell).
England (Playing XI) - Jamie Smith, Ben Duckett, Jos Buttler (WK), Harry Brook (C), Tom Banton, Jacob Bethell, Will Jacks, Liam Dawson, Brydon Carse, Adil Rashid, Luke Wood (In for Matthew Potts).
TOSS - England win the toss and they will BOWL first.

Right then, not the biggest of grounds in Bristol and when you glance over the two batting lineups, you think it will be raining 4s and 6s throughout the whole game. This then makes the bowling and fielding side of things even more crucial, as that could be the area that makes all the difference in an expected high-scoring affair. Can West Indies bounce back and get some momentum going for them? Or will England find a way to blow them away yet again? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

West Indies simply haven't had things their way on this tour and even before taking on England, they seemed a bit shaky against Ireland. They have lost the ODI series 3-0 already and will be desperate for a win here before heading into the final game of the tour. The Windies have big T20 names throughout their lineup but need more consistency and that is what is separating them from the best teams right now. Also, with Akeal Hosein finally sorting out his visa issues, he will be expected to not only be in the team, but will be expected to play a huge role with the ball.

England seem to have regained their lost white ball prowess in this series as they won the ODI series 3-0 and were clinical when it mattered in the 1st T20I as well. With the weight of captaincy lifted, Jos Buttler seems rejuvenated and that long batting lineup can be a handful for any bowling attack in the world. However, the hosts will be hoping that more players in that stacked middle order perform instead of just making up the numbers.

Hello and welcome to the Seat Unique Stadium in Bristol, where England will be taking on West Indies in the 2nd T20I of this series. Hosts England have already taken a 1-0 lead but they will be eyeing to seal the series win before heading to Southampton, whereas the Windies will be looking to find some crucial form on an thus far inconsistent tour with a win. It should be an exciting game to watch.
... MATCH DAY ...

From Chester-le-Street, the caravan moves south to Bristol for the second T20I of the three-match series between England and West Indies. Much like the ODI leg, the hosts have taken an early lead and will be looking to seal the series when they take the field at the Seat Unique Stadium. In the opening game, Jos Buttler led the charge with a superb 96, guiding England to a total of 188. At the halfway mark, it looked slightly below par, but the English bowlers stepped up and ensured it was more than enough. The likes of Ben Duckett, Harry Brook and Tom Banton failed to make an impression and will be eager to get among the runs. With the ball, Liam Dawson marked his return to T20Is for the first time since 2022 with a match-winning four-wicket haul. Brydon Carse and Adil Rashid kept things tight, while debutant Matthew Potts had a tough outing and will be keen to bounce back in Bristol. For West Indies, there were a few positives despite the result. After being put under the pump in the Powerplay, they managed to pull things back and keep England under 190. The absence of Akeal Hosein due to visa issues was clearly felt, and there is still uncertainty over his availability for the remainder of the series. Alzarri Joseph had a forgettable outing, going for plenty, and will be looking to redeem himself in the second game. With the bat, Evin Lewis looked promising at the top, but there was not much to write home about the rest. The likes of Johnson Charles, Shai Hope, Sherfane Rutherford and Rovman Powell will need to fire collectively if the tourists are to keep the series alive. With a quick turnaround and plenty to prove, can the Men in Maroon land a counterpunch and take the series to a decider? We shall find out together.
